newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 hits record high ahead of futures expiry.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 hits record high ahead of futures expiry.

text.p: Derivative-related trading ahead of Friday's expiry of FTSE 100 and mid-250 futures and options pushed leading shares to a fresh high in early afternoon trade on Thursday, traders said.
The FTSE 100 climbed 31.1 points to 3,986.8, a rise of 0.79 percent on the day. The new high narrowly beats the previous best of 3,986.7 set on September 17.
"Underlying business is thin, there's a short position in the futures and that's what's driving us up, but not much underlying cash business," said one trader.
Volumes were a modest 329 million with most businesss driven by market-makers looking to protect themselves against violent swings in share prices at tomorrow's derivatives expiry.
Dealers said the psychologically-important 4,000 level remains a possibility by the end of the week.
A revival of bid talk also helped lift shares, with Zeneca surging 86.5p to a new high of 16.30 stg on rumours it may be the target of Germany's Bayer AG.

Rumours of a bid for Zeneca have abounded since its split from ICI three years ago, though none has yet proved to have any substance. "If the Zeneca bid does appear, that could be the catalyst to see us through 4,000," said one trader.
But dealers remain divided on whether shares have either the momentum or confidence to push ahead much further.
While some warn the 4,000 level could provide the signal for investors to take profits, others points to the historically high institutional cash levels as the fuel to take shares even higher.
"There is too much cash waiting to go in, funds are too liquid and there is nowhere else to put the money," commented one senior London trader.
